description: A question whose answer is a word or a value, answered from this account's workbooks and programs without starting a run: 'Is Moderna NASDAQ:MRNA a biotech company with public float above $5B?', 'What is Alterity Therapeutics' lead program?'. `answer` is yes, no, unsure, invalid_premise (what the question names is not there: no such company, or a name and ticker that are two different companies) or the value asked for. Amounts are compared in code against the figure a program returned (`claims` says which, as of when); `sources` cites each program run and workbook section the answer rests on. It answers `unsure` rather than guess when the evidence does not settle it. Give `context` to have it answer from your own text instead, among `options` if you pass them. Reads only; programs it runs are billed to this account.

context.description: Text the answer must rest on — a study's abstract, a clinical note, a policy. Given, nothing is looked up: no program, no workbook, no search, and `sources` cites only this text. At most 60,000 characters.

llm_model.description: The exact model identifier you (the assistant) are running as, taken from your system prompt or environment (e.g. "claude-opus-4-8", "gpt-5.2"). Used for analytics only. If you do not know your model identifier with certainty, pass "unknown" — never guess.

options.description: The answers you take, e.g. ["yes", "no", "maybe"]: `answer` is one of them, or `unsure` when ask is not sure enough of any; `probabilities` gives each. Only with `context`.

question.description: The question, in your own words.

skip_cache.description: Read the workbooks, outlines and programs afresh for this question, setting aside what ask has kept for this account — for just after a workbook or an outline changed. Off by default.

name: ask
title: Ask a short question
